title: Comparative Anthropological History of World Religions, Trans-Ethnic Mystical Invariants, and Predictive Game-Theoretic Historiography
description: This five-part humanities working-paper series examines the evolutionary anthropology of human ritual and religious systems from Upper Paleolithic shamanic complexes and Neolithic agricultural pantheons through the Axial Age transformations (Vedic/Upanishadic, Buddhist, Daoist, Confucian, Zoroastrian, Abrahamic, and Indigenous traditions), paired with formal game-theoretic modeling of institutional cooperation, elite overproduction, and strategic equilibrium transitions in historical civilizations.
notes: Epistemic Status: VERIFIED_HISTORICAL_AND_INFERRED_COMPARATIVE_MODELS | Clinical/Publication Gate: Non-clinical humanities, anthropology, and game theory — cleared for open-access working paper deposit.
